parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The pagination cursor token used to retrieve the next set of records.

Capture the `nextCursor` from the response JSON and provide it here to continue fetching data.


**The 10-Second Rule:** Due to QuickBooks Desktop architectural requirements, you must request
the next page within **10 seconds** of receiving the previous response.


**Static Cursors:** Unlike some APIs, the cursor remains constant for the entire duration
of the fetch sequence until `hasMore` is `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more unique identifiers (ListIDs).

Provide a list of strictly matched ListIDs. This is the most efficient way to retrieve specific records.

parameters.name: fullNames
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more exact full names.

Returns records whose `FullName` exactly matches any of the provided strings.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: updatedBefore
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or before this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **23:59:59** (end of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or after this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **00:00:00** (beginning of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description:
Filter by name (substring match).

Matches records where the `FullName` contains this string.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: nameStartsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name starts with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` begins with this string.
Example: Searching "Mac" returns "MacPherson", "MacGyver", etc.

parameters.name: nameEndsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name ends with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` finishes with this string.
Example: Searching "kitchen" returns "John's Kitchen", "Central Kitchen", etc.

parameters.name: nameFrom
parameters.description:
Name range filter (start).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or after this value.

parameters.name: nameTo
parameters.description:
Name range filter (end).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or before this value.
If both `nameFrom` and `nameTo` are specified, `nameTo` must be lexicographically higher.

parameters.name: IncludeRetElementList
parameters.description:
Limit the response to only these top-level fields. Names must match exactly (case-sensitive QbXML element names e.g. ListIDRet, NameRet, AddressRet, PhoneRet  ).

**Note:** The names specified in the list are not parsed, so you must be especially careful to supply valid
names, properly cased. No error is returned in the status code if you specify an invalid name. Notice that if you want to
return custom data or private data extensions, you must specify the DataExtRet element and you must supply the OwnerID set
to either a value of 0 (custom data) or the GUID for the private data.
<example>["ListIDRet", "NameRet", "AddressRet", "PhoneRet"]</example>

parameters.name: ActiveStatus
parameters.description: Shortcut for Filters.ActiveStatus - Filter by active status enum: ActiveOnly InactiveOnly ALL

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The pagination cursor token used to retrieve the next set of records.

Capture the `nextCursor` from the response JSON and provide it here to continue fetching data.


**The 10-Second Rule:** Due to QuickBooks Desktop architectural requirements, you must request
the next page within **10 seconds** of receiving the previous response.


**Static Cursors:** Unlike some APIs, the cursor remains constant for the entire duration
of the fetch sequence until `hasMore` is `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more unique identifiers (ListIDs).

Provide a list of strictly matched ListIDs. This is the most efficient way to retrieve specific records.

parameters.name: fullNames
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more exact full names.

Returns records whose `FullName` exactly matches any of the provided strings.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: activeStatus
parameters.description: Shortcut for Filters.ActiveStatus - Filter by active status enum: ActiveOnly InactiveOnly ALL

parameters.name: updatedBefore
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or before this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **23:59:59** (end of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or after this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **00:00:00** (beginning of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description:
Filter by name (substring match).

Matches records where the `FullName` contains this string.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: nameStartsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name starts with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` begins with this string.
Example: Searching "Mac" returns "MacPherson", "MacGyver", etc.

parameters.name: nameEndsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name ends with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` finishes with this string.
Example: Searching "kitchen" returns "John's Kitchen", "Central Kitchen", etc.

parameters.name: nameFrom
parameters.description:
Name range filter (start).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or after this value.

parameters.name: nameTo
parameters.description:
Name range filter (end).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or before this value.
If both `nameFrom` and `nameTo` are specified, `nameTo` must be lexicographically higher.

parameters.name: IncludeRetElementList
parameters.description:
Limit the response to only these top-level fields. Names must match exactly (case-sensitive QbXML element names e.g. ListIDRet, NameRet, AddressRet, PhoneRet  ).

**Note:** The names specified in the list are not parsed, so you must be especially careful to supply valid
names, properly cased. No error is returned in the status code if you specify an invalid name. Notice that if you want to
return custom data or private data extensions, you must specify the DataExtRet element and you must supply the OwnerID set
to either a value of 0 (custom data) or the GUID for the private data.
<example>["ListIDRet", "NameRet", "AddressRet", "PhoneRet"]</example>

parameters.name: X-Connection-Id
parameters.description:
Identifies which QuickBooks Desktop company file to target.

Accepts three formats:
- **Prefixed ID**: `conn_01965a3f2e7b7000b4c1d2e3f4a5b6c7`
- **Internal GUID**: `3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6`
- **Your external ID**: `acme-corp` (the `externalId` you assigned when creating the connection)

The middleware resolves any of these formats to the correct connection. Required for all QuickBooks resource operations — without it, the API cannot determine which company file to query.

parameters.name: X-Correlation-ID
parameters.description:
A unique identifier for tracing a single request through the entire system.
If not provided by the client, a new one will be generated.
This is not persisted and is used only for logging and monitoring.

parameters.name: X-Nxus-Timeout-Seconds
parameters.description:
Maximum time in seconds to wait for the queued job to be picked up and the response returned from QuickBooks Desktop.

List and streaming query operations accept **1–90** seconds (default **90**). Raise this when the QuickBooks Web Connector is configured with longer polling intervals or the target company file is slow to respond.

Passed as a request header — not a query-string value.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of ItemSalesTaxs where the default limit is 150.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The pagination cursor token used to retrieve the next set of records.

Capture the `nextCursor` from the response JSON and provide it here to continue fetching data.


**The 10-Second Rule:** Due to QuickBooks Desktop architectural requirements, you must request
the next page within **10 seconds** of receiving the previous response.


**Static Cursors:** Unlike some APIs, the cursor remains constant for the entire duration
of the fetch sequence until `hasMore` is `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more unique identifiers (ListIDs).

Provide a list of strictly matched ListIDs. This is the most efficient way to retrieve specific records.

parameters.name: fullNames
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more exact full names.

Returns records whose `FullName` exactly matches any of the provided strings.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: activeStatus
parameters.description: Shortcut for Filters.ActiveStatus - Filter by active status enum: ActiveOnly InactiveOnly ALL

parameters.name: updatedBefore
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or before this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **23:59:59** (end of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or after this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **00:00:00** (beginning of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description:
Filter by name (substring match).

Matches records where the `FullName` contains this string.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: nameStartsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name starts with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` begins with this string.
Example: Searching "Mac" returns "MacPherson", "MacGyver", etc.

parameters.name: nameEndsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name ends with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` finishes with this string.
Example: Searching "kitchen" returns "John's Kitchen", "Central Kitchen", etc.

parameters.name: nameFrom
parameters.description:
Name range filter (start).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or after this value.

parameters.name: nameTo
parameters.description:
Name range filter (end).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or before this value.
If both `nameFrom` and `nameTo` are specified, `nameTo` must be lexicographically higher.

parameters.name: IncludeRetElementList
parameters.description:
Limit the response to only these top-level fields. Names must match exactly (case-sensitive QbXML element names e.g. ListIDRet, NameRet, AddressRet, PhoneRet  ).

**Note:** The names specified in the list are not parsed, so you must be especially careful to supply valid
names, properly cased. No error is returned in the status code if you specify an invalid name. Notice that if you want to
return custom data or private data extensions, you must specify the DataExtRet element and you must supply the OwnerID set
to either a value of 0 (custom data) or the GUID for the private data.

parameters.name: X-Connection-Id

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The pagination cursor token used to retrieve the next set of records.

Capture the `nextCursor` from the response JSON and provide it here to continue fetching data.


**The 10-Second Rule:** Due to QuickBooks Desktop architectural requirements, you must request
the next page within **10 seconds** of receiving the previous response.


**Static Cursors:** Unlike some APIs, the cursor remains constant for the entire duration
of the fetch sequence until `hasMore` is `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more unique identifiers (ListIDs).

Provide a list of strictly matched ListIDs. This is the most efficient way to retrieve specific records.

parameters.name: fullNames
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more exact full names.

Returns records whose `FullName` exactly matches any of the provided strings.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: activeStatus
parameters.description: Shortcut for Filters.ActiveStatus - Filter by active status enum: ActiveOnly InactiveOnly ALL

parameters.name: updatedBefore
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or before this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **23:59:59** (end of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or after this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **00:00:00** (beginning of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description:
Filter by name (substring match).

Matches records where the `FullName` contains this string.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: nameStartsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name starts with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` begins with this string.
Example: Searching "Mac" returns "MacPherson", "MacGyver", etc.

parameters.name: nameEndsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name ends with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` finishes with this string.
Example: Searching "kitchen" returns "John's Kitchen", "Central Kitchen", etc.

parameters.name: nameFrom
parameters.description:
Name range filter (start).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or after this value.

parameters.name: nameTo
parameters.description:
Name range filter (end).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or before this value.
If both `nameFrom` and `nameTo` are specified, `nameTo` must be lexicographically higher.

parameters.name: IncludeRetElementList
parameters.description:
Limit the response to only these top-level fields. Names must match exactly (case-sensitive QbXML element names e.g. ListIDRet, NameRet, AddressRet, PhoneRet  ).

**Note:** The names specified in the list are not parsed, so you must be especially careful to supply valid
names, properly cased. No error is returned in the status code if you specify an invalid name. Notice that if you want to
return custom data or private data extensions, you must specify the DataExtRet element and you must supply the OwnerID set
to either a value of 0 (custom data) or the GUID for the private data.
<example>["ListIDRet", "NameRet", "AddressRet", "PhoneRet"]</example>

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The pagination cursor token used to retrieve the next set of records.

Capture the `nextCursor` from the response JSON and provide it here to continue fetching data.


**The 10-Second Rule:** Due to QuickBooks Desktop architectural requirements, you must request
the next page within **10 seconds** of receiving the previous response.


**Static Cursors:** Unlike some APIs, the cursor remains constant for the entire duration
of the fetch sequence until `hasMore` is `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more unique identifiers (ListIDs).

Provide a list of strictly matched ListIDs. This is the most efficient way to retrieve specific records.

parameters.name: fullNames
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more exact full names.

Returns records whose `FullName` exactly matches any of the provided strings.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: activeStatus
parameters.description: Shortcut for Filters.ActiveStatus - Filter by active status enum: ActiveOnly InactiveOnly ALL

parameters.name: updatedBefore
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or before this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **23:59:59** (end of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or after this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **00:00:00** (beginning of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description:
Filter by name (substring match).

Matches records where the `FullName` contains this string.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: nameStartsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name starts with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` begins with this string.
Example: Searching "Mac" returns "MacPherson", "MacGyver", etc.

parameters.name: nameEndsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name ends with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` finishes with this string.
Example: Searching "kitchen" returns "John's Kitchen", "Central Kitchen", etc.

parameters.name: nameFrom
parameters.description:
Name range filter (start).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or after this value.

parameters.name: nameTo
parameters.description:
Name range filter (end).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or before this value.
If both `nameFrom` and `nameTo` are specified, `nameTo` must be lexicographically higher.

parameters.name: IncludeRetElementList
parameters.description:
Limit the response to only these top-level fields. Names must match exactly (case-sensitive QbXML element names e.g. ListIDRet, NameRet, AddressRet, PhoneRet  ).

**Note:** The names specified in the list are not parsed, so you must be especially careful to supply valid
names, properly cased. No error is returned in the status code if you specify an invalid name. Notice that if you want to
return custom data or private data extensions, you must specify the DataExtRet element and you must supply the OwnerID set
to either a value of 0 (custom data) or the GUID for the private data.
<example>["ListIDRet", "NameRet", "AddressRet", "PhoneRet"]</example>

parameters.name: X-Connection-Id
parameters.description:
Identifies which QuickBooks Desktop company file to target.

Accepts three formats:
- **Prefixed ID**: `conn_01965a3f2e7b7000b4c1d2e3f4a5b6c7`
- **Internal GUID**: `3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6`
- **Your external ID**: `acme-corp` (the `externalId` you assigned when creating the connection)

The middleware resolves any of these formats to the correct connection. Required for all QuickBooks resource operations — without it, the API cannot determine which company file to query.

parameters.name: X-Correlation-ID
parameters.description:
A unique identifier for tracing a single request through the entire system.
If not provided by the client, a new one will be generated.
This is not persisted and is used only for logging and monitoring.

parameters.name: X-Nxus-Timeout-Seconds
parameters.description:
Maximum time in seconds to wait for the queued job to be picked up and the response returned from QuickBooks Desktop.

List and streaming query operations accept **1–90** seconds (default **90**). Raise this when the QuickBooks Web Connector is configured with longer polling intervals or the target company file is slow to respond.

Passed as a request header — not a query-string value.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of ItemSubtotals where the default limit is 150.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The pagination cursor token used to retrieve the next set of records.

Capture the `nextCursor` from the response JSON and provide it here to continue fetching data.


**The 10-Second Rule:** Due to QuickBooks Desktop architectural requirements, you must request
the next page within **10 seconds** of receiving the previous response.


**Static Cursors:** Unlike some APIs, the cursor remains constant for the entire duration
of the fetch sequence until `hasMore` is `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return per page.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more unique identifiers (ListIDs).

Provide a list of strictly matched ListIDs. This is the most efficient way to retrieve specific records.

parameters.name: fullNames
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more exact full names.

Returns records whose `FullName` exactly matches any of the provided strings.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: activeStatus
parameters.description: Shortcut for Filters.ActiveStatus - Filter by active status enum: ActiveOnly InactiveOnly ALL

parameters.name: updatedBefore
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or before this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **23:59:59** (end of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: updatedAfter
parameters.description:
Filter for records modified on or after this date.

**Time Defaults:** If a time is not specified, local time **00:00:00** (beginning of day) is assumed.


**Range:** Supports dates from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-18.

parameters.name: nameContains
parameters.description:
Filter by name (substring match).

Matches records where the `FullName` contains this string.
Case-insensitive according to QuickBooks Desktop rules.

parameters.name: nameStartsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name starts with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` begins with this string.
Example: Searching "Mac" returns "MacPherson", "MacGyver", etc.

parameters.name: nameEndsWith
parameters.description:
Return records whose name ends with this value.

Matches records where the `FullName` finishes with this string.
Example: Searching "kitchen" returns "John's Kitchen", "Central Kitchen", etc.

parameters.name: nameFrom
parameters.description:
Name range filter (start).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or after this value.

parameters.name: nameTo
parameters.description:
Name range filter (end).

Returns records whose name is alphabetically at or before this value.
If both `nameFrom` and `nameTo` are specified, `nameTo` must be lexicographically higher.

parameters.name: IncludeRetElementList
parameters.description:
Limit the response to only these top-level fields. Names must match exactly (case-sensitive QbXML element names e.g. ListIDRet, NameRet, AddressRet, PhoneRet  ).

**Note:** The names specified in the list are not parsed, so you must be especially careful to supply valid
names, properly cased. No error is returned in the status code if you specify an invalid name. Notice that if you want to
return custom data or private data extensions, you must specify the DataExtRet element and you must supply the OwnerID set
to either a value of 0 (custom data) or the GUID for the private data.

parameters.name: X-Connection-Id

parameters.name: X-Connection-Id
parameters.description:
Identifies which QuickBooks Desktop company file to target.

Accepts three formats:
- **Prefixed ID**: `conn_01965a3f2e7b7000b4c1d2e3f4a5b6c7`
- **Internal GUID**: `3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6`
- **Your external ID**: `acme-corp` (the `externalId` you assigned when creating the connection)

The middleware resolves any of these formats to the correct connection. Required for all QuickBooks resource operations — without it, the API cannot determine which company file to query.

parameters.name: X-Nxus-Timeout-Seconds
parameters.description:
Maximum time in seconds to wait for the queued job to be picked up and the response returned from QuickBooks Desktop.

Create / update / delete and single-entity retrieval operations accept **1–120** seconds (default **120**). Raise this when the QuickBooks Web Connector is configured with longer polling intervals or the target company file is slow to respond.

Passed as a request header — not a query-string value.

post.summary:
Tells the backend that the client is done consuming the given paginated cursor.
The SOAP iterator-continuation hold (up to ~10s waiting for the next "continue")
unblocks immediately, the QWC lane frees, and the underlying job is marked
`Completed` by the SOAP side.

Idempotent: calling on an unknown / already-closed cursor returns 204 with no
observable side effect. Safe for SDK `finally` blocks and user-driven retry.

Tenant-scoped: only signals when the live session belongs to the caller's tenant.
Cross-tenant requests silently return 204 (do NOT leak whether the cursor existed).

post.summary:
Creates an auth session for a connection, returning a ready-to-use `authFlowUrl`.

Send this URL to your user — they will download the QuickBooks Web Connector config file
and follow the on-screen steps to activate the connection.
post.description:
**Typical flow:**
1. Create a connection in the portal (or via `POST /api/v1/connections`) and note its `connectionId`.
2. When your user is ready to connect QuickBooks, call this endpoint with that `connectionId`.
3. Redirect or link your user to the returned `authFlowUrl` — they complete the QWC setup from there.
   Creating a new auth session expires any older pending or in-progress setup links for that connection.
4. Poll `GET /api/v1/qwc-auth-setup/{connectionId}/status/authenticated` until `isConnected = true`.

**connectionId** — accepts the prefixed ID returned by `GET /api/v1/connections`,
a raw GUID, or your configured `externalId`.

**redirectUrl** (optional) — where to send the user after the QWC setup page completes.

**linkExpiryMins** (optional) — how long the auth setup URL remains valid, in minutes.
Defaults to 30 minutes. Maximum allowed value is 10,080 minutes (7 days).

post.summary:
Creates a new QuickBooks Desktop connection.

After creating a connection, call `POST /api/v1/auth-sessions` with the
returned `id` to generate an auth setup URL for your user.
post.description:
**mode** — for API-key-authenticated requests, mode is derived from the key type:
`sk_test_*` creates development connections and `sk_live_*` creates
production connections. Cookie-authenticated management requests still honor the
request body's `mode` value.
Production connections are created immediately, but remain non-operational until
Stripe billing is completed. The response includes billing redirect details.

**externalId** — your own identifier for this connection (e.g. your customer or user ID).
Must be unique within your account. Once set, it can be used anywhere a
`connectionId` is accepted, so you never need to store our internal IDs.

- Your own `externalId`: e.g. `acme-corp`

get.summary:
Returns the current tenant's profile.
Includes the publishable key (pk_nxus_live_...) for use in hosted QWC auth flow URLs.
get.description:
The publishable key is a stable, tenant-level credential used as the ?pk= query parameter
when directing end users to your hosted QWC setup page:

  https://yourapp.com/connect/{connectionId}?pk={publishableKey}

Unlike the secret API key, the publishable key is safe to embed in client-side code.
It does NOT rotate when you rotate secret API keys.
Use POST /api/v1/tenant/me/rotate-publishable-key to intentionally rotate it.

name.description: Account name (required)

fullName.description: The fully-qualified unique name for this object, formed by combining the names of its parent objects with its own `name`, separated by colons. Not case-sensitive. Parent:Child:SubChild

parent.description: The short name of the account as it appears in the QuickBooks UI.

sublevel.description: Depth level of the account in the hierarchy (0 for top level).

accountType.description: The specific type of the account.

isTaxAccount.description:
Whether the account is a tax account (optional, default: false)
Only set to true for accounts that track tax liabilities/expenses

bankNumber.description: Bank account number (for bank accounts only)

description.description: Description of the account. Maps to 'Desc' in XML.

salesTaxCode.description:
Reference to the associated Sales Tax Code.
Derived from SalesTaxCodeRef.

cashFlowClassification.description: Cash flow classification for the account.

currency.description:
Reference to the currency associated with the account.
Derived from CurrencyRef.

isActive.description: Whether the account is active (default: true)

Account.description: A QuickBooks Desktop Account object is a type of List object that represents a financial account within a company's chart of accounts, such as a Bank, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, or Credit Card account Because it is a list object, it is tracked and identified by a unique, QuickBooks-assigned ListID as well as a FullName.

AccountTaxLineInfo.description:
DTO representing Account Tax Line Information.
Used to map accounts to federal tax lines.

AccountType.description:
Defines the valid Account Types for QuickBooks Desktop.
The specific type of the account, such as Bank, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, CreditCard, etc.

relation.description: Relation for emergency contacts only. Values: Spouse, Partner, Mother, Father, Sister, Brother, Son, Daughter, Friend, Other

noteId.description: The ID of the note to modify (required for updates).

AdditionalNote.description:
Request model for adding a new additional note (EmployeeAdd).
Per DTD: AdditionalNotes just has Note element.

Address.description: Address data model - shared across all QuickBooks entities

AddressBlock.description:
Represents the 5-line address block for check printing.
Corresponds to the AddressBlock XML element.

note.description: (Optional) A note associated with the address.

AddressRequest.description: A reusable request DTO for an address block.

ApplicableCredit.description: Represents a credit that can be applied to a bill.

paymentAmount.description:
Monetary amount of the payment in the transaction's currency.

Uses decimal for financial precision. Null indicates the amount is unspecified.

setCredits.description:
Collection of requests to set credits.

May be null. Initialized at object creation (init-only). Serialized as
"setCredits".

discountAmount.description:
Monetary amount of any discount applied to the item or transaction.

Null when no discount is applied. Use the same currency and scale as other monetary values in
the model.

discountAccountId.description:
Identifier of the account used for discounts.

Nullable; null indicates no discount account is assigned. When present, it should correspond
to an account identifier in the accounting system.

discountClassId.description:
Identifier of the discount class.

Corresponds to the JSON property "discountClassId". May be null when no discount class is
assigned.

AppliedToTransactionRequest.description:
Request model for AppliedToTxn line items.
Represents an invoice or transaction that this payment is being applied to.

refNumber.description: The primary reference number for the transaction this one is applied to.

balanceRemaining.description: The balance remaining on the applied-to transaction.

paymentAmount.description: The amount of the parent transaction applied to this one.

discountAmount.description: The discount amount given on the applied-to transaction.

discountAccount.description: Reference to the discount account used.

discountClass.description: Reference to the class used for the discount.

AppliedToTxn.description:
Represents a transaction that a parent transaction (e.g., a Payment) has been applied to.
This element is typically found in response objects like ReceivePaymentRet or BillPaymentCheckRet.

amount.description:
The amount of the check to apply to this transaction.
(Optional - if not specified, QuickBooks will apply the full check amount)

ApplyCheckToTransactionRequest.description:
Represents the ApplyCheckToTxnAdd aggregate in QBXML (SIMPLER structure for CheckAdd only).
Used for applying a check as a direct refund to customer transactions.
This is the simplified version with only TxnID and Amount.

paymentAmount.description:
The amount of the payment to apply to this transaction.
(Optional in schema, but typically used)

appliedCredits.description:
List of credits to set/apply to this transaction.
(Optional, may repeat)

discountAmount.description:
The amount of discount to apply.
(Optional)

discountAccountId.description:
The account to track the discount.
(Optional)

discountClassId.description:
The class to track the discount.
(Optional)

isValid.description: Validation: Must specify either PaymentAmount, AppliedCredits, DiscountAmount, or any combination.

ApplyToTransactionRequest.description:
Represents the AppliedToTxnAdd aggregate in QBXML (FULL structure for BillPayments).
Used for applying a payment or credit to a specific transaction (e.g., in BillPaymentCreditCardAdd, BillPaymentCheckAdd).
This is the complex version with credits and discounts.

exchangeRate.description: (Optional) The exchange rate for the transaction.

refNumber.description: (Optional) The reference number for the refund.

refundAppliedToTxns.description: (Required) List of credit transactions (e.g., Credit Memos) to apply this refund to.

ArRefundCreditCard.description:
Adds a credit card refund transaction that is linked to one or more QuickBooks credit memo transactions.
You can link the credit card refund to one or more of those credit transactions. Notice that this provides 
functionality over and above what the UI provides, which currently allows a user to link only one credit 
card refund to one credit transaction.

createdAt.description: UTC timestamp when this session was created

connectionId.description: The connection ID this session was created for

clientSecret.description:
Opaque secret for server-side session identification.
Do not share this with your users.

authFlowUrl.description:
The URL to send your user to for QWC setup.
Embed this in an email, button, or redirect — the user clicks it,
walks through the setup wizard, and the connection activates.

expiresAt.description:
UTC timestamp when this session expires.
Defaults to 30 minutes from creation. Extend with `linkExpiryMins`.

redirectUrl.description: The redirect URL included in the request, if any

AuthSessionResponse.description:
A short-lived auth session containing the URL to send your user to
complete QuickBooks Desktop connection setup.

listType.description: ListType may have one of the following values: Account, Class, Customer, CustomerMsg, CustomerType, DateDrivenTerms, Employee, ItemDiscount, ItemFixedAsset, ItemGroup, ItemInventory, ItemInventoryAssembly, ItemNonInventory, ItemOtherCharge, ItemPayment, ItemSalesTax, ItemSalesTaxGroup, ItemService, ItemSubtotal, JobType, OtherName, PaymentMethod, PriceLevel, SalesRep, SalesTaxCode, ShipMethod, StandardTerms, ToDo, Vendor, VendorType

BarCode.description: Represents a Barcode identifier associated with a QuickBooks List Object (e.g., Item, Customer, Vendor).

assignEvenIfUsed.description: (Optional) If true, allows the value to be assigned even if already in use.

allowOverride.description: (Optional) If true, allows the bar code value to be overridden in transactions.

BarCodeRequest.description:
Contains optional BarCode settings for SpecialItemAdd.
Corresponds to the BarCode aggregate.

name.description: The case-insensitive unique name of this base unit, unique across all base units. **NOTE**: Base units do not have a `fullName` field because they are not hierarchical objects, which is why `name` is unique for them but not for objects that have parents. Maximum length: 31 characters.

abbreviation.description: The base unit's short identifier shown in the QuickBooks U/M field on transaction line items. Maximum length: 31 characters.

BaseUnit.description: DTO for the base unit of a UnitOfMeasureSet.

name.description: (Required) The name of the base unit (e.g., "Barrel"). Max length: 31.

abbreviation.description: (Required) The abbreviation of the base unit (e.g., "bbl"). Max length: 31.

BaseUnitRequest.description:
Defines the required base unit settings for a new UnitOfMeasureSet.
Maps to the QBXML BaseUnit element.

QBXML Schema Constraints:
- Name: Required, max length = 31
- Abbreviation: Required, max length = 31

vendor.description:
The vendor who issued the bill. When linking to a Purchase Order, this vendor
must match the vendor on the Purchase Order.

vendorAddress.description: The billing address of the vendor.

dueDate.description: The date by which the bill must be paid.

amountDue.description: The total monetary amount of the bill.

exchangeRate.description: Exchange rate for multi-currency transactions (v8.0).

amountDueInHomeCurrency.description:
The total amount due expressed in the company's home currency.
This is calculated and returned by QuickBooks when the multicurrency feature is enabled.

refNumber.description: Reference number for the bill.

isPending.description: Indicates whether the bill is currently marked as pending.

terms.description: The payment terms associated with the bill (e.g., Net 30), which calculate the DueDate.

class.description:
The class associated with the bill, used for categorizing expenses and reporting
(requires class tracking to be enabled in QuickBooks).

salesTaxCode.description: The sales tax code indicating the general taxability of the bill (e.g., Tax, Non).

isPaid.description: Indicates whether the bill has been paid in full and closed.

isTaxIncluded.description: Indicates whether the amounts in the bill already include sales tax.

expenseLines.description:
Expense line items for the bill.
At least one expense line or item line is required.

itemLines.description: Item line items for the bill (for inventory items).

Bill.description:
An Accounts Payable (A/P) transaction representing a bill received from a vendor. 
Bills increase the amount owed to a vendor and impact the specified A/P account. 
When creating a new bill, it can be linked to existing Purchase Orders to automatically 
pull in line item data and update the Purchase Order's status to received.
Note: In some QuickBooks editions (such as Enterprise), preference settings may require 
the use of transaction dates, meaning TxnDate must be supplied even if marked optional.

name.description: (Required) The name of the billing rate.

billingRateType.description: Indicates whether the billing rate applies a fixed rate to all service items or custom rates per individual service item [2-4].

fixedBillingRate.description: A simple fixed rate that will override all the standard rates for service items performed by the entity assigned this billing rate [2, 3].

billingRatePerItems.description: A list of specific service items that are being overridden by a fixed custom rate or percentage [2, 4].

BillingRate.description:
A list object representing a billing rate, which is a custom price that overrides the standard price set for a service item, based on the entity (employee or vendor) that does the work [1, 2]. 
This allows you to charge different rates based on who does the work or the difficulty of the task [1].

itemId.description: (Required) The ListID or FullName of the service item to override.

CreditCardBill.description:
Represents a transaction where a credit card is used to settle one or more outstanding vendor bills.
In accounting terms, this shifts a liability from the Accounts Payable (A/P) account to the credit card's balance.
A key feature is the explicit link created between this payment and the specific bills it covers,
which is essential for accurate payment tracking and maintaining correct vendor balances within QuickBooks.

Customer.description:
Customers:
A customer record in QuickBooks represents either a business or individual who purchases goods or services, or a specific job/project being performed for that customer. 
Jobs are treated as sub-customers; they inherit billing information from their parent customer while allowing for job-specific details to be tracked.

InventoryItem.description:
Inventory are things the QuickBooks company sells, as well as things it buys. QuickBooks Desktop can manage product inventory. Line items entered on sales, 
purchase, and refund transactions flow into inventory items to automatically adjust quantity on hand. Additionally, cost and price of individual inventory 
items are stored so inventory value can be tracked. After enabling inventory management, add individual inventory items as Item objects. 
QuickBooks Supports: 
FIFO inventory accounting, Tracking quantity on hand, Categories to four levels, Taxable status of the item, Price and cost

Item.description:
Any line item on a purchase order, invoice, or estimate must be set up as an Item.
Items act as pointers for the financial statements.In other words, items handle the behind the scenes accounting for sales and purchases.
Items make it easier to fill out sales forms.
Items allow you to track quantities purchased and sold in addition to dollars purchased and sold.

ItemItemNonInventory.description: Materials or parts for which you do not track quantities. Materials or parts you buy but do not sell, or materials or parts you sell but do not buy, are non-inventory items. For example, if you sell a service that requires a part, but you do not want to track the part as an inventory item, you can set up the part as a non-inventory item. You can also use non-inventory items for one-time purchases or sales of items that you do not want to track at all. Non-inventory items are used on sales forms and purchase forms, and they affect your financial statements.

ItemItemSalesTaxGroup.description:
Sales-tax group item, is an item used for calculating two or more sales taxes grouped 
together and applied to the same sale. 

For example, local and state taxes could be tracked 
separately but applied to a sale as one tax. (Compare with the ItemSalesTaxAdd message.) Taxes 
can be reflected in transaction line items The following information refers to invoices 
specifically, but it also applies to sales receipts. Generally its best to assign a tax item 
or tax group item to an invoice and allow QuickBooks to apply the same tax to all taxable 
items on the invoice. However in some situations multiple tax combinations are required, so 
this method doesn’t work. In this case one must use techniques to apply the taxes in the 
invoice itself as line items.

ItemReceipt.description:
Represents an Item Receipt transaction DTO.
This inherits TxnID, RefNumber, TxnDate, Amount (from TotalAmount), 
Entity (from VendorRef), Memo, ExchangeRate, AmountInHomeCurrency,
ExternalGuid, and all line item lists from BaseTransactionDto.
An item receipt records the physical receipt of inventory items from a vendor. It can be linked 
to a purchase order to automatically update inventory quantities and close out the purchase order. 
When linked, line items are automatically pulled from the purchase order, eliminating the need to 
recreate them manually. This linking can only be done during item receipt creation, 
not during modification.

ItemSalesTaxGroup.description:
Sales-tax group item, is an item used for calculating two or more sales taxes grouped 
together and applied to the same sale. 

For example, local and state taxes could be tracked 
separately but applied to a sale as one tax. (Compare with the ItemSalesTaxAdd message.) Taxes 
can be reflected in transaction line items The following information refers to invoices 
specifically, but it also applies to sales receipts. Generally its best to assign a tax item 
or tax group item to an invoice and allow QuickBooks to apply the same tax to all taxable 
items on the invoice. However in some situations multiple tax combinations are required, so 
this method doesn’t work. In this case one must use techniques to apply the taxes in the 
invoice itself as line items.

id.description: The unique nexus identifier for the report object in the REST API.

Report.description:
Generic QuickBooks Report object (e.g., Aging, Custom).
A report is a method for obtaining a comprehensive view of data across multiple objects and over a specified time period, as opposed to a query, which typically just provides a simple snapshot of specific objects.
 Reports are capable of spanning multiple data types and can be customized in a wide variety of ways.
 When QuickBooks returns a report response, it generally contains two main types of information:
 Report Meta-data: This information describes the report as a whole.
 It includes the report's title and subtitle, the report basis (such as Cash, Accrual, or None), the total number of rows and columns, the number of rows used for column titles, and a column descriptor for each column that outlines its ID, title, column type, and data type.
 Report Data: This is the actual content, presented as sequential rows of data expressed in name/value pairs.
 These rows are further categorized into four types: text rows (mainly used for headings), data rows(the core report data), subtotal rows(calculated subtotals), and a single total row(the calculated total for the entire report).
